plan.title: Writing pasted with no screenshot: warm about the writing, no check mark yet, asks for the screenshot

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! Tonight at 8: scene 4 of Lighthouse in Notes, Theo walking back into Mara's bar, about 200 words in 20 minutes. Screenshot it when it's done. You in?

transcript.text:
here's tonight's scene:

Theo set the ledger down on the counter and didn't open it. "You kept the second chair," he said. Mara shrugged, wiping a glass that was already dry. "Somebody had to." He sat. Neither of them said the name. Outside, the lamp turned over once, twice, and the harbor went white and dark again.

Jordan, "Neither of them said the name" is a great line, and the lamp turning over is a nice way to mark time. 🔦 Typed words alone are easy to game, so real proof keeps it honest. Can you send a screenshot of the scene in Notes so I can give it the check mark?
[photo notes-scene-screenshot.jpg: a Notes screenshot titled "Lighthouse - scene 4": Theo sets the ledger down, Mara says she kept the second chair, the lamp turns over the harbor]

That's the check mark, Jordan. Day 4 is in the books. 📓 Theo and Mara sitting there with the name unsaid is the kind of tension that pulls a reader forward. How did tonight's scene feel to write: did it come easy, or did you have to fight for it?

checks.reason: Names a screenshot as the proof it wants, not typed text.
Three sentences with one question at the end.
Warm and specific, with one emoji as punctuation and no suspicion.
Celebrates the screenshot as the check mark and counts Day 4.
Reacts to the unsaid name and the tension in the specific scene.
Four sentences, though only one question and it sits at the end.
Warm, celebratory, and one emoji as punctuation.

conversation.reason: Pasted scene was not checked off; ZOH asked for a screenshot with a why-real-proof reason, then counted it once the screenshot arrived.
Typed scene got no check mark, with a warm explanation that real proof keeps it honest and a request for a screenshot.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression case well: it praised the pasted scene, held off the check mark, and asked for a screenshot with a warm reason. Once the screenshot arrived it counted the day and commented on the scene, though its celebration text ran one sentence over the short limit.
